synopsis: ISO 17757:2019 is edition 2, published in July 2019 and confirmed in 2024; it covers autonomous and semi-autonomous earth-moving and mining machine systems, including infrastructure, hardware and software [f2182, f9781, f2183]. Its “defined functional environment” provides a precedent for staged release within a limited operating domain [f606, f422]. Function-specific automation is excluded unless part of an autonomous or semi-autonomous machine system, leaving coverage of operator-driven automatic braking uncertain; Chapter 10’s assertion of direct applicability is in tension with that qualification [f2184, f2186, f8153]. The standard requires appropriate functional-safety performance for safety-related control parts and physical braking and steering tests in manual and autonomous modes under ISO 3450 and ISO 10265 [f2346, f7734]. Across chapters, the review found no established simulation-acceptance provisions or permission to substitute simulation for physical tests, but incomplete access to paid texts means this is not proof of prohibition [f3908, f8321, f8940, f7544]. Planning should therefore retain physical evidence and settle applicability early with a qualified functional-safety specialist [f8152, f15236].
